title: What training and qualification does EU GMP Annex 1 require for sterile manufacturing staff?
seoTitle: EU GMP Annex 1 sterile staff training
description: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) personnel rules for sterile sites: cleanroom training, annual gowning requalification and aseptic process simulation participation.
shortAnswer: Annex 1 of the EU GMP Guide (Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products, revised 2022) requires everyone entering cleanrooms, including cleaning, maintenance and monitoring staff, to receive regular training, gowning qualification and assessment. Staff entering grade A and B areas must pass a gowning assessment, repeated at least annually with visual and microbial checks, and must have taken part in a successful aseptic process simulation before working unsupervised. Each operator must join at least one successful simulation every year.
keyTakeaways: The revised Annex 1 was published in EudraLex Volume 4 in August 2022 and came into operation on 25 August 2023, except paragraph 8.123 on lyophilizer loading, which followed on 25 August 2024.

Paragraph 7.3 extends cleanroom training to cleaning, maintenance and monitoring personnel, and sets core content: microbiology basics, hygiene, cleanroom practices, contamination control, aseptic technique and patient safety implications.
Aseptic gowning must be assessed and reassessed at least annually, using both visual and microbial assessment at sites such as gloved fingers, forearms, chest and hood.

Unsupervised grade A and B access requires a passed gowning assessment and participation in a successful aseptic process simulation (APS). Each operator should take part in at least one successful APS annually.
There must be a documented disqualification route: adverse monitoring trends or a failed APS lead to retraining and requalification before further aseptic work.
jurisdiction: European Union (EU Member States; the guideline is jointly maintained with PIC/S)
regulator: European Commission (EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 1), with GMP inspections by the national competent authorities of the Member States
appliesTo: Manufacturers of sterile medicinal products for human and veterinary use, including investigational medicinal products
All personnel who access cleanrooms, including operators, cleaning, maintenance and environmental monitoring staff
Operators who enter grade B or intervene in grade A, and those performing manual aseptic operations
Visual inspection operators and personnel who read APS units

sections.heading: What is Annex 1 and when did the 2022 revision take effect?

blocks.text: Annex 1 is the sterile manufacturing supplement to the EU Guidelines for Good Manufacturing Practice, and its 2022 revision has applied since 25 August 2023. The European Commission adopted the text as [C(2022) 5938 final](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/e05af55b-38e9-42bf-8495-194bbf0b9262_en?filename=20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf), dated 22 August 2022, replacing the 2007 version. It came into operation one year after publication in EudraLex Volume 4, with paragraph 8.123 following two years after publication, on 25 August 2024.

Annex 1 was revised jointly by the EU GMP/GDP Inspectors Working Group and the PIC/S Committee, so the same personnel requirements apply in PIC/S member countries. It builds on the general personnel rules in [EU GMP Chapter 2](/regulations/eu-gmp-chapter-2-personnel-training-requirements); paragraph 2.22 of Chapter 2 points to the annexes for special product groups such as sterile preparations. For the Australian implementation of the same text, see [TGA GMP personnel training requirements](/regulations/tga-gmp-personnel-training-requirements). The requirements summarized here are those in force as at November 2026.

Section 7 (Personnel) gives "guidance on the requirements for specific training, knowledge and skills" and on the qualification of personnel. Training also appears in production, aseptic process simulation, visual inspection and quality control sections, which this page brings together.

sections.heading: Who needs cleanroom training under Annex 1?

blocks.text: Anyone who enters a cleanroom needs training, not only aseptic operators. Paragraph 7.3 states:

blocks.title: Annex 1, paragraph 7.3 (extract)
blocks.text: "All personnel including those performing cleaning, maintenance, monitoring and those that access cleanrooms should receive regular training, gowning qualification and assessment in disciplines relevant to the correct manufacture of sterile products."

The training should include basic microbiology and hygiene, with a specific focus on cleanroom practices, contamination control, aseptic techniques and the protection of sterile products for those entering grade B or intervening in grade A, and the potential safety implications to the patient if the product is not sterile. The level of training should be based on the criticality of the function and the area. Paragraph 7.1 also requires sufficient personnel who are qualified, trained and experienced in sterile manufacture and testing and in the specific technologies used at the site.

Unqualified personnel should not enter grade B cleanrooms or grade A in operation (7.5). In exceptional cases, a written procedure must govern their entry, an authorized person must supervise them and assess the impact on cleanliness, and the access must be recorded under the pharmaceutical quality system.

sections.heading: How often must gowning be requalified?

blocks.text: At least annually. Paragraph 7.4 requires personnel accessing grade A and B areas to be trained in aseptic gowning and aseptic behaviors, with compliance confirmed by assessment and periodic reassessment at least annually, involving both visual and microbial assessment.

The microbial assessment uses monitoring locations such as gloved fingers, forearms, chest and hood (facemask or forehead), against the limits in paragraph 9.30. Table 6 sets glove print action limits of no growth for grade A and 5 CFU per glove for grade B. Gowning itself must follow a written procedure (7.10), garments must be checked for cleanliness and integrity before and after gowning (7.11), and operators entering grade A or B must put on clean, sterilized garments at each entry (7.15).

Paragraph 7.18 asks for slow, controlled and methodical movement in clean areas and suggests that a review of airflow visualization studies be considered as part of the training program. Paragraph 8.19 requires aseptic operations, including APS, to be observed regularly by people with specific aseptic expertise, to verify operator behavior and correct inappropriate practices.

sections.heading: How does aseptic process simulation participation work for operators?

blocks.text: Operators qualify through APS (media fill) participation, and keep their qualification by taking part again every year. Paragraph 7.4 restricts unsupervised access to grade A and B areas where aseptic operations are conducted to personnel who "have passed the gowning assessment and have participated in a successful APS."

items: **Routine lines (9.38):** APS is normally repeated twice a year (approximately every six months) for each aseptic process, filling line and shift, and "each operator should participate in at least one successful APS annually."

**Manual aseptic operations (9.39):** where filling or compounding is manual, each operator should initially take part in at least 3 consecutive successful APS for each container type, closure and equipment train, then be revalidated with one APS approximately every 6 months.

**Interventions (9.34 and 8.17):** APS should include inherent and corrective interventions at a representative frequency, and batch records should document interventions with time, duration and the operators involved.
**Maximum headcount (7.2):** the maximum number of operators in cleanrooms should be determined, documented and considered during initial qualification and APS.
**Failed APS (9.46 vi):** where a failure is linked to operator activity, that operator's activities should be limited until retrained and requalified.

blocks.title: Disqualification and requalification (7.6)
blocks.text: Sites must have a system to disqualify personnel from cleanroom work or unsupervised entry, based on ongoing assessment, adverse trends in personnel monitoring, or involvement in a failed APS. Retraining and requalification must be completed before further aseptic work, and for grade B and grade A operators requalification should consider participation in a successful APS.

sections.heading: Which other roles need specific qualification?

blocks.text: Visual inspectors, APS readers and quality control microbiology staff have their own qualification expectations. These are easy to miss because they sit outside section 7.

items: **Manual visual inspection (8.31):** operators should undergo visual inspection qualification at least annually, wearing corrective lenses if they normally do, using samples from the defect library and worst-case conditions such as inspection time, line speed, container size or fatigue. Qualification should include consideration of eyesight checks.
**Defect library (8.30):** a defect library capturing all known defect classes should be maintained and used for training production and quality assurance personnel.
**APS unit inspection (9.45):** filled APS units should be inspected by personnel trained and qualified to detect microbiological contamination.

**Quality control (10.1):** personnel with appropriate training and experience in microbiology, sterility assurance and process knowledge should be available to support design, environmental monitoring and investigations.
**Health reporting (7.7):** personnel should be instructed to report health conditions that may cause abnormal shedding of contaminants.

blocks.text: A gowning or APS qualification is a form of [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) rather than completion tracking. The setup steps are in [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency), and the matrix method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each Annex 1 qualification, such as gowning, APS participation and visual inspection, as an assessment point linked to the roles and areas it governs and to the contamination control strategy that sets its depth. Expiring or revoked qualifications can then be traced to the access rights and roles they affect. See the [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences) page for context.

faqs.q: Does Annex 1 require every operator to do a media fill every six months?
faqs.a: Not for routine automated lines. Paragraph 9.38 says APS is normally repeated about every six months per process, line and shift, and each operator should take part in at least one successful APS annually. The six-monthly per-operator expectation applies to manual aseptic operations under paragraph 9.39.

faqs.q: Do grade C and D staff need gowning qualification?
faqs.a: Paragraph 7.3 says all personnel who access cleanrooms should receive regular training, gowning qualification and assessment relevant to sterile manufacture, at a level based on the criticality of their function and area. The annual visual and microbial gowning reassessment in paragraph 7.4 is specific to grade A and B access.

faqs.q: What happens when an operator fails a gowning assessment?
faqs.a: The operator should not have unsupervised access to grade A or B areas until requalified. Paragraph 7.6 requires a disqualification system based on ongoing assessment and monitoring trends, with retraining and requalification completed before further aseptic work. For grade B and grade A work, requalification should consider APS participation.

Annex 1 is guidance that interprets the binding GMP principles in Directive (EU) 2017/1572 and, for veterinary products, the corresponding legislation. Inspectors use it as the standard for sterile manufacturing, and deviations need a documented, risk-based justification that achieves at least the same level of assurance.
